title: Composite types, constructors and nested mutability
outcome: Use owned types to represent data contracts and distinguish immutable bindings from recursively immutable state.

exercises.title: Validate a unit
exercises.task: Attempt to construct a measurement with an unsupported unit.
exercises.hint: Check the invariant before new creates the object.
exercises.answer: Field types alone cannot distinguish supported and unsupported physical units.

exercises.title: Inspect conversion
exercises.answer: The conversion is deliberate and can have precision consequences for other numeric inputs.

exercises.title: Try field reassignment
exercises.task: Reassign a field of an immutable measurement.
exercises.hint: The struct field binding is fixed after construction.
exercises.answer: This says nothing about whether the original measurement was scientifically valid.

exercises.title: Mutate nested storage
exercises.expected: Its contents can change despite the immutable outer struct.
exercises.answer: Deep immutability requires more than an immutable wrapper.

exercises.title: Create a snapshot
exercises.task: Copy the vector before storing it in another record.
exercises.expected: Later source-vector mutation does not affect that copied vector.
exercises.hint: Choose the required storage independence explicitly.
exercises.answer: A snapshot policy must account for every nested mutable layer.

exercises.title: Review a convenience constructor
exercises.task: Add a constructor with a default unit in an owned copy.
exercises.expected: It preserves the same validation contract.
exercises.hint: Route convenience paths through validated construction.
exercises.answer: An API becomes inconsistent if one creation path bypasses its stated invariant.
